title: A photodynamical model with the measured Be-star orbit fits the 1990-2026 eclipses of HD 93683: the Be star alone drives the eclipse loss at 28 deg mutual inclination and mass fraction B = 0.735
abstract: HD 93683 is an eclipsing O9V+B0V pair (P = 17.8 d) whose eclipses faded from 1990 to 2026. Prior campaign studies measured the orbit of a Be star around the pair (P2 = 890.5 d) with VLTI/GRAVITY and velocities, but the mutual inclination and the mass fraction B = m(pair)/m(total) stayed open (estimates 0.63, <= 0.83, 0.905). We fitted a photodynamical model (REBOUND three-body integration with the outer orbit fixed, light-travel time and a GR apsidal term, eclipse light curves from the sky positions) to 6,955 Tycho (1990-1993), ASAS-3 (2000-2009) and TESS (2019-2026) points with a fixed noise model. With 12 parameters it gives chi2 = 1,991, against 2,326 for the empirical model of the source study (12 parameters) and 2,207 for a 16-parameter empirical control with light-travel time and quadratic terms. All four data sets fit better. Of eight drift-consistent geometry families, one fits (all others Delta chi2 >= 247): mutual inclination 28 deg (26.7-29.4 deg oscillation), inner node 333 deg from the outer node. The B profile gives B = 0.735 (0.71-0.745 at Delta chi2 = 1) and excludes 0.63, 0.83 and 0.905 (Delta chi2 = 97, 175, 1,297). This gives 16.3 + 13.6 and 10.8 solar masses and 2.28 kpc, close to the Carina distance. A fit to TESS alone converges to the same solution and predicts the 2000-2009 ASAS-3 data as well as an empirical fit to those data. The Tycho timing offset of the source study falls from -0.25 d to -0.05 d. The model predicts a 415-yr precession cycle and the next eclipses near 2240. Limits: fixed outer orbit, fixed noise model without MCMC, no stellar spin or tides, constant third light.

citations.reason: We reuse its eclipse model, data selection, error model and TESS event table; our dynamical model replaces its linear inclination drift and removes most of its Tycho timing offset.
We fix the outer orbit at its GRAVITY and Fe II solution and answer its open question on the mutual inclination; our B = 0.735 excludes its wide-companion reflex value 0.905.
We use its K(Be) = 59.18 km/s in a test and compare its disentangling coupling q = 0.59 (B = 0.63) with our B.
Discovery of the eclipse loss; we read its ASAS-3 point table.
A second signed version of the GRAVITY study with the same orbit.
Its outer-period limit agrees with the dynamical solution.
Its companion-mass floor agrees with m(Be) = 10.8 solar masses.
